title: Sales Mitarbeiter – Teilzeit / Werkstudent
description: Unsere Mission Wir bei DeWarmte sind davon überzeugt, dass die Energiewende nur dann funktioniert, wenn sie für alle zugänglich und attraktiv ist. Dieser Kerngedanken leitet uns bei DeWarmte. Deshalb entwickeln und installieren wir unsere eigenen Wärmepumpen. So machen wir nachhaltiges Heizen intelligenter, bezahlbarer und für immer mehr Haushalte zugänglich. Wir sind ein schnell wachsendes Unternehmen und bauen aktuell unser Geschäft in NRW aus mit einem neuen Standort in Düsseldorf. Wir leben kurze Entscheidungswege, offene Kommunikation und einen starken Teamgeist. Dir wird Vertrauen und Verantwortung entgegengebracht – und gleichzeitig die Unterstützung, die du benötigst, um erfolgreich zu sein. Deine Aufgaben Wir wachsen rasant und immer mehr Menschen finden den Weg zu uns. Deshalb suchen wir eine/n Mitarbeiter/in für die Leadqualifizierung, der/ die dafür sorgt, dass jeder interessierte und bestehende Kunde schnell und kompetent betreut wird. Du stehst mit Kunden in Kontakt, hauptsächlich telefonisch und per Video. Du hörst gut zu, stellst die richtigen Fragen und hilfst dem Kunden, den logischen nächsten Schritt zu gehen. Manchmal bedeutet das, einen Termin für eine digitale Inspektion zu vereinbaren. Manchmal stellt sich heraus, dass unsere Lösung nicht passt. Du musst bei deinem Einstieg kein Wärmepumpen-Experte sein. Wichtig ist uns jedoch, dass du neugierig bist, schnell lernst und Energie aus dem intensiven Kundenkontakt schöpfst. Du befasst dich mit: Telefonischer Erstkontakt zu potenziellen Kunden Nachverfolgung und Qualifizierung neuer Leads Bestehende Kunden bei Fragen weiterhelfen und für eine gute Nachbetreuung sorgen Gespräche und Termine ordentlich in unserem CRM-System erfassen Rückrufvereinbarungen und offene Aufgaben eigenständig nachverfolgen Erkennen, wo Kunden auf Schwierigkeiten stoßen, und diese Erkenntnisse mit dem Team teilen Dein Profil Für diese Position ist uns deine Arbeitsweise wichtiger als ein bestimmter Abschluss oder eine bestimmte Anzahl an Jahren Berufserfahrung. Du knüpfst leicht Kontakte, hörst gut zu, stellst gezielte Fragen und kannst Informationen auf einfache Weise erklären. Außerdem verfügst du über kommerziellen Ehrgeiz. Es macht dir Spaß, ein Gespräch in die richtige Richtung zu lenken und du traust dich, einen konkreten nächsten Schritt vorzuschlagen. Du bist überzeugend, ohne aufdringlich zu sein. Du findest schnell heraus, was jemand sucht, wie die Situation aussieht und ob es sinnvoll ist, den Prozess fortzusetzen. An einem geschäftigen Tag sprichst du mit verschiedenen Kunden. Das gibt dir eher Energie, als dass es dich abschreckt. Und du arbeitest strukturiert und selbstständig. Wenn du jemandem versprichst, am Donnerstag zurückzurufen, dann tust du das auch. Erfahrung im Vertrieb ist schön, aber sicherlich nicht der einzige Weg zu dieser Stelle. Vielleicht hast du im Inbound-Vertrieb, im Telefonverkauf, in einem Callcenter, in der Energiebranche oder in der Telekommunikation gearbeitet. Aber auch Erfahrungen im Gastgewerbe können sehr relevant sein, wenn du dort gelernt hast, schnell Kontakt aufzubauen, gut zuzuhören und kommerziell zu denken. Dabei helfen dir: Interesse an Technik und Nachhaltigkeit Erfahrung mit Beratungsgesprächen oder Videokonferenzen fließende Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse Digitale Skills, z. B. im Umgang mit CRM-Systemen wie HubSpot Wir erwarten nicht, dass du vom ersten Tag an über technisches Wissen zu Wärmepumpen verfügst. Wir bringen dir bei, was du wissen musst. Wir erwarten jedoch, dass du neugierig bist und neue Informationen schnell aufnimmst. title: Technical Deployment Manager
description: Artificial Intelligence. Actual Impact. At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses. We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart : trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive. So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops. 🚀 The Adventure Ahead Step into the driver’s seat of customer transformation as our next Technical Deployment Manager, where no two integrations or customer journeys look the same! In this hybrid technical-consulting role, you will be the architectural backbone and trusted advisor guiding global organizations through complex onboarding milestones, bespoke workflows, and seamless platform connectivity. You'll bridge the gap between high-level customer vision and deep technical execution, directly unlocking the full power of Docebo’s AI-driven learning suite for enterprise teams around the globe. If you love solving technical puzzles, building automated workflows, and delivering tangible "aha!" moments to customers, your next big career adventure starts right here. 🛠️ The Day-to-Day Lead the Charge: Partner directly with diverse, global enterprise clients to translate ambitious business objectives into crystal-clear technical success criteria and project roadmaps. Architect the Integrations: Design, configure, and troubleshoot robust API workflows and enterprise product add-ons, including Single Sign-On (SSO) and web conferencing tools. Automate the Magic: Build cutting-edge data transfer workflows and third-party platform connections via Docebo Connect using Workato-powered middleware technology. Unlock Deep Insights: Craft and deploy custom SQL queries directly into customer platforms to deliver actionable, high-impact reporting. Bridge the Strategy: Collaborate seamlessly across Sales Engineering, Professional Services, and Customer Success to keep cross-functional stakeholders aligned and projects on budget. Pave the Trail: Produce and refine top-notch technical documentation and deployment best practices that turn complex configurations into repeatable wins. Navigate the Horizon: Proactively uncover, quantify, and mitigate technical risks early to guarantee smooth, friction-free onboarding experiences every time. ⚡ Your Superpowers Consulting & SaaS Savvy: Proven track record in customer-facing SaaS environments (2+ years) with solid grounding in software implementation and technical consulting (4+ years relevant experience overall). Technical Chops: Hands-on experience working with REST APIs, testing web services with HTTP clients like Postman, and a working foundation in SSO protocols and SQL. Integration Fluency: Working knowledge of automation middleware platforms (such as Workato, Zapier, or MuleSoft) with an aptitude for building clean data flows. Curiosity & Fast Learning: A boundless appetite for mastering new technologies, digging deep into platform mechanics, and evolving into a go-to Docebo product authority. Customer-First Communication: Exceptional relationship-building skills with the ability to ask the right questions, understand nuanced needs, and turn technical jargon into clear business value. Global Fluency: Professional bilingual proficiency in both spoken and written English and German, paired with an openness to travel occasionally (10% or less). 🌟 Bonus Points Identity & Code Expertise: Advanced experience with SAML or OpenID Connect, alongside hands-on coding ability in at least one modern programming language. Enterprise Ecosystem Know-How: Background navigating large-scale enterprise deployments and integrating complex HRIS, CRM, or enterprise calendar ecosystems. Multilingual Flair: Professional working proficiency in additional languages such as Italian, French, or Spanish. Our Total Rewards Philosophy 🎉 Our Total Rewards Philosophy centers around three core areas to reward and care for our People: Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success. Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being. Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul. Our Promise to You 😍 Financial Wellness: Own a piece of Docebo through our Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) at a 15% discount, plus a competitive compensation package. Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it. Rest, Relax, Repeat: Rest and recharge with paid vacation days, two company-wide Docebo Days, floating holidays for cultural celebrations, and your birthday off! Family First : We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025! Connections That Count: Connect with global communities through our Employee Resource Groups (including PRIDE, DWA, BIDOC, and Green Ambassadors) and company-wide events that keep the fun rolling all year long. About Docebo 💙 At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. We have successfully achieved two IPOs ( TSX: DCBO & NASDAQ: DCBO ), been recognized as a top SaaS e-learning solution, and are growing exponentially in the process. We're a global company, with office across North America, EMEA, APAC, and beyond. Our team is guided by five core values— Grow Together Win Together, Build with Our Customer, Clear is Kind, Own Outcomes, Progress Over Perfection —that shape everything we do. If this resonates with you, now is the perfect time to join one of the fastest-growing learning technology companies in the world. Docebo is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer . We are committed to diversity and inclusion in our workforce. All qualified applicants and employees will receive consideration for employment regardless of their race, colour, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, genetic information, or any other category protected under applicable law. As a federal contractor, Docebo is committed to the principles of affirmative action and equal employment opportunity for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Docebo does not discriminate because of protected veteran status or on the basis of disability, and Docebo takes affirmative action to employ and advance in employment qualified protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Any individuals requiring a reasonable accommodation or would like to voluntarily disclose a disability or protected veteran status to assist with their employment application should send an e-mail to their recruiter directly. description: About Griffin Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences. We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more. We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies. Learn more about what we do Our culture We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible. We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life. We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified. Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers. Learn more about our culture. The team Infrastructure sits within the Craft function. We’re a small team of three - two engineers and an engineering manager - who work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner . It’s our job to build the foundations that everything else at Griffin runs on: the systems, the tooling, the automation that helps us run a highly resilient and reliable platform and lets other teams ship fast. We're a software engineering team as much as an infrastructure team: we write the code that runs our platform, not just the configuration around it. When we start work, we explore multiple solutions before picking one. We write RFCs, build proof-of-concepts, and run experiments to validate approaches. Once we commit to building something, we care about maintainability more than cleverness, observability more than hoping it works, and scalability over premature optimisation. We take the necessary time to ship quality solutions rather than hitting arbitrary deadlines. Once something goes live, we refactor the rough edges rather than polish what's already working. The opportunity Day to day, you'll build and manage the infrastructure the bank runs on - both in the cloud and on our own hardware in third party data centres. This means running FoundationDB clusters and writing the software and tooling for hitless upgrades, managing Kubernetes, writing infrastructure as code in Pulumi and CDK, running the Bazel build farm, and owning the deployment pipeline from CI to production. Operational resilience is a big part of the job: replica clusters, multi-region failover, and chaos engineering to test how systems handle failures. Security access, CircleCI pipelines, DataDog integration, and cloud spend all fall under infrastructure too. On our roadmap currently is: building out our self-hosted infrastructure to support a hybrid-cloud setup and remove single-vendor reliance, improving how Kubernetes scales, improving the build farm, and building out our PKI infrastructure. We also have plans for a global HTTP routing layer to allow seamless failover between sites. Much of this is software we built ourselves, and you'll shape it from the first design through to production. Our infrastructure as code is written in TypeScript. Where it makes sense, tooling gets written in Clojure. There's some Rust too. What success looks like Infrastructure problems become production problems fast. Success here means thinking ahead - identifying issues with scale, security, or compliance before they affect services. You've eliminated an entire class of incidents by fixing the underlying architectural issue. You've proven the database and compute platform can handle 10x current traffic volumes by working with backend teams to stress-test it. You've cut deploy times in half by rethinking how the pipeline works. You've tested multi-region failover under realistic failure scenarios and it worked. You've shipped well-tested software that turns risky manual operations, like database upgrades, into routine, hitless ones that the whole team maintains with confidence. You've redesigned service discovery to remove networking issues that used to cause weekly firefights. When new FCA requirements dropped, you were already compliant because you'd built the infrastructure to handle it months earlier. To do this, you'll own Infrastructure architecture decisions - how we structure our systems, what approaches we take, what tools we build Production reliability - keeping the database, compute, build farm, and deployment pipelines running and improving them What other teams depend on to ship - CI/CD, security access, monitoring integration, and the infrastructure that lets engineers deploy safely Infrastructure cost and efficiency - managing spend and resource usage across AWS and DataDog Infrastructure software - the code behind our database control plane, operational tooling and automation, from design and implementation through to testing, code review and maintenance Stack: FoundationDB, Kubernetes, Bazel, Pulumi, CDK, CircleCI, DataDog, Clojure, TypeScript Your background You'll fit in well here if you have: Solid systems experience - you've run container orchestration in production, written infrastructure as code, and understand IP networking well enough to debug it when things go wrong Cloud infrastructure experience - you've built and managed production environments, worked with networking, identity management, and compute at scale Strong software engineering fundamentals - you write code to solve problems, and you're as comfortable designing, testing and reviewing production software as you are configuring infrastructure. TypeScript, Python, Go, or functional languages are all fine. If your experience only extends to Bash scripting and YAML, we probably aren't a good fit for you Comfort with startup environments - small teams, shifting priorities, high autonomy We write a lot of our tooling in Clojure - our database control plane, operational scripts, and automation. You don't need Clojure experience coming in, but you'll need to learn it once you're here. If you've worked with functional languages before, that helps. Regardless, you should be comfortable picking up new languages and approaches as we do find ourselves reading through the codebases of open-source systems and tools we use to understand their behaviour, and they are written in a diverse range of languages we don't use ourselves. What can we offer you? We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future. Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment. As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks. How do I apply? Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next. We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs. Under representation At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. You work daily with the safety (software) engineers and with TÜV to define what must be verified. Early on, you set up and prove the verification system for the current system, and you then carry it into the certification of the new controller.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own the verification of our new safety controller end to end, from the verification plan to the certification evidence (target PL d per ISO 13849-1:2023 and SIL 2 per IEC 61508)

  • Build the complete verification catalog and set up the verification process and structure from scratch

  • Verify the safety software at unit and integration level with automated tests including fault and robustness cases, structural coverage, static analysis, and code and requirement reviews

  • Automate verification so that it runs on every change

  • Verify the controller and its safety functions as part of the robot arm against ISO 10218-1:2025

  • Keep traceability from risk assessment to test results and write reports that hold up in an audit

  • Work closely with the safety (software) engineers and TÜV to define what must be verified

  • Review the verification work of your colleagues and share your practices with the team

We're looking for someone who has:

  • A degree in a technical field such as software, electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent experience

  • 3+ years of experience verifying or testing safety-critical embedded systems in industrial automation, automotive, rail, aerospace or medical devices

  • Enough embedded C to write white-box tests and to find defects in a code review

  • Working knowledge of IEC 61508-3 or its industry counterpart (ISO 26262-6, EN 50716, DO-178C) and the verification evidence it requires

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

The Role

This is not a traditional procurement role. At Andercore, procurement is trading: fast-paced, market-driven, and executed daily — not on quarterly or annual cycles. You will lead a team of young and hungry category managers, through high-volume purchasing decisions in a dynamic environment where prices, availability, and supplier landscapes shift constantly.

You will own end-to-end procurement strategy and execution: sourcing, onboarding to the system, supplier negotiations and disputes, pricing, team leadership, and process design. We need someone who can think strategically and execute operationally every single day — from setting category strategy to approving individual purchase orders. You will be in the driver seat to build the first AI automated trading engine - a unique opportunity in the industrial supply space.

You report directly to the C level and sit on the commercial and operations leadership team. Andercore uses AI extensively across the business; you will be expected to leverage it to drive efficiency, margins, and scalability in procurement.

The core purpose of this role is to build one buying strategy that combines three things:

  • Spot trading, run as a repeatable system with a regular market-coverage schedule and clear KPIs;

  • Strategic buying, where you negotiate allocations, framework agreements and terms with Tier-1 manufacturers and develop private-label and direct-from-factory categories;

  • Supply planning, where you set the mix of spot, contract and stock and keep price and inventory risk under control.

Each part on its own is not enough. The job is to make them work together so that Andercore buys at the right price, secures supply when the market tightens, and never holds stock it cannot sell.

  • Build and run the procurement machine: Develop and execute procurement strategies that support an 8-digit monthly procurement spend with exponential growth. Negotiate favourable terms, pricing, and contracts with suppliers on a daily basis.

  • AI-native procurement: automate processes from RFQs through to order confirmations, with sellers as co-designers of the agents.

  • Revenue and margin targets consistently met or exceeded through high availability and competitive pricing.

  • A robust, high-quality supplier network with strong retention and engagement across existing and emerging markets.

  • Streamlined, repeatable processes that reduce time-to-onboard, minimise errors, and allow the team to scale without linear headcount growth.

  • A high-performing, motivated team with emerging team leads and strong cross-functional collaboration.

  • Accurate, data-driven reporting that drives continuous improvement and informs executive strategy.

  • Run a category management that unlocks and owns new product lines

Who You Are

Must-Haves

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree from a top university or business school.

  • 4+ years in a high-performance environment: for example commodity trading / high-velocity B2B procurement.

  • Proven ability to build processes and delegate effectively. You must be able to create systems that outlast your personal involvement — not do everything yourself.

  • Strong assertiveness and people leadership. You will manage a young team that needs clear direction, daily prioritisation, and coaching.

  • Ability to operate at both strategic and granular levels: setting category strategy in the morning and reviewing individual POs in the afternoon.

  • Excellent analytical and communication skills.

  • Fluent English is required; German is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable with a high-intensity, fast-paced startup environment where priorities can shift daily.

  • Proven results negotiating from the smaller side of the table, i.e. securing allocation, pricing and terms when you are not the biggest customer.

  • Hard-working, proactive, and independent. Willing to go the extra mile to get the job done.

  • A personal track record in spot or commodity trading with margin ownership.

  • Experience scaling a team, plus forecasting and inventory risk management.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in marketplaces, SaaS, or construction / infrastructure / energy materials.

  • Exposure to AI-driven operations or automation of procurement workflows.

  • Familiarity with cross-border trade and international supplier management.

  • Tier-1 strategy consulting background (e.g. McKinsey, BCG, Bain).

  • Your procurement experience is in slow-cycle, enterprise purchasing (annual contracts, quarterly reviews). Our cadence is daily.

  • You are strong on analysis but weak on implementation. We need someone who executes, not just diagnoses.

  • You prefer to do things yourself rather than build teams and processes. Delegation and system-building are non-negotiable.

title: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
description: Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. Protect applications in a fundamental way so that developers can build great application services and not be constantly looking over their shoulder. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security. The role Location: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North Carolina You will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them. The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?). This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right. Working with design delivered as code At BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review. This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening. Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready. Roles and collaboration Software development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture. In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design. What you'll do Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes. Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them. Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events. Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint. Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI. Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done. Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen. Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing. When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review. Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow. How we expect you to work These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool. Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix. Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later. Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill. Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it. Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review. Our UI stack and design system Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders. All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own. A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI. Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it. What you bring About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens. An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load. Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI. Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem. A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it. Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally. Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce. CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped. Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens. Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing. Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates. Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products. Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that. Your first 90 days First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer. Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component. Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening. About BlueRock: BlueRock is a well-funded, early stage cybersecurity company founded by experienced security minded entrepreneurs. Our mission is to change the game in cybersecurity. Attackers are exploiting in hours. The dependency tree is exploding. Developers are drowning in vulnerability debt. BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.

In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.

What you'll do

  • Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.

  • Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.

  • Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.

  • Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.

  • Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.

  • Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.

  • Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.

  • Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.

  • When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.

  • Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.

How we expect you to work

These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.

  1. Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.

  2. Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.

  3. Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.

  4. Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.

  5. Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.

Our UI stack and design system

Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.

All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.

A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.

  • Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite

  • Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes

  • Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages

  • Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views

  • Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI

  • Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags

  • Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux

You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.

What you bring

  • About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.

  • An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.

  • Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.

  • Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.

  • A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.

  • Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.

  • Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.

  • CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.

  • Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.

  • Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.

  • Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.

Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.

Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.

Your first 90 days

  1. First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.

  2. Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.

  3. Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.

Die WTE Group baut Unternehmen gegen den Fachkräftemangel. Mit WTE Charkos bringen wir Pflege- und Kita-Fachkräfte aus Indien nach Deutschland, mit B2-Deutsch vor dem ersten Gespräch und eigenem Ausbildungszentrum in Mysore. Unsere Kunden sind unter anderem Universitätskliniken, und jede Vermittlung besetzt eine Stelle in Pflege oder Kita und bedeutet einen Neustart für einen Menschen. Was Du machst Du begleitest internationale Fachkräfte von der Zusage bis zum ersten Arbeitstag. Du stellst Unterlagen für Anerkennung und Visum zusammen und prüfst sie. Du koordinierst Termine mit Behörden, Arbeitgebern und Unterkünften. Du bist Ansprechperson für Kliniken, Pflegeheime und unser Team in Indien. Du organisierst das Onboarding vor Ort und setzt klare Prozesse um, mit KI (Claude) als Werkzeug. Was Du mitbringst Ein abgeschlossenes Studium. Die Fachrichtung ist offen, Berufserfahrung brauchst Du nicht. Du arbeitest strukturiert und zuverlässig. Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch. Lust, mit KI zu arbeiten. Was wir bieten 36.000 bis 45.000 € brutto im Jahr, je nach Erfahrung und Kenntnissen. Neues Büro in Hamburg, kleines Team und direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den beiden Gründern. Früh eigene Verantwortung und gründliche Einarbeitung, damit Du nach kurzer Zeit eigene Fälle sicher betreust. KI-gestütztes Arbeiten mit Claude ab Tag 1. Teams in Hamburg und Indien, bei denen Du viel über internationale Zusammenarbeit lernst. Bewirb Dich in 2 Minuten mit Deinem Lebenslauf. Ein Anschreiben brauchst Du nicht. Client management, consultative communication, or provider-facing education experience preferred. Tech Lead (Perm, USA, Remote + Travel)

This is a full-time, permanent opportunity for candidates based in the United States and authorized to work without sponsorship. Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

This position also requires traveling to client sites within the U.S., with travel expenses covered by the company.

About Nearform

Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.

As part of our Engineering function, you will work closely with clients to translate complex business requirements into innovative digital products.
Whether you are a Senior Engineer, Tech Lead, or DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate with distributed teams, leveraging cutting-edge technologies to build secure, high-performance applications. Our Nearform engineers are known for building high quality, scalable solutions that solve real world problems.

About the Technical Lead Role:

As a Technical Lead at Nearform, you will be responsible for leading and guiding development teams while working directly with clients to translate business and technical requirements into impactful applications. However, as you’ll likely work on a variety of projects in your time here, your responsibilities may also include:

  • Provide technical and line-management leadership to your development team.
  • Take responsibility for the successful delivery of projects.
  • Identify and resolve blockers before they become issues.
  • Ensure best practices in software development, DevOps, and agile methodologies are upheld within the team.
  • Work directly with clients, translating requirements into technical briefs.
  • Shape and define architectural decisions ensuring scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Provide updates to client and Nearform leadership to ensure clear understanding of project status and drive good decision-making.

What we are looking for in this person:

  • Significant experience in software engineering and 2+ years of experience leading projects and mentoring as a Technical Lead. For this particular role, we are looking for professional experience with Python and React.
  • Experience with AI application development and Agentic frameworks and platforms (e.g., LangGraph, Agentspace, etc.)
  • Experience working directly with clients or customers to understand technical requirements.
  • Strong CI/CD experience, including hands-on work with Terraform, Helm, and other cloud-native IaC technologies.
  • Experience leading software engineering teams through technical delivery and either direct line management or mentoring.
  • Deep understanding of agile ways of working, best practices and design patterns.
  • Deep understanding of test-driven development and testing best practices.
  • Deep understanding of version control tools, e.g. Git.
  • Understanding of DevOps practices and cloud technologies (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Understanding of operational concerns (such as monitoring, performance testing, security considerations, accessibility, GDPR)
  • Empathy and people skills

Benefits & Perks:

  • Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance.
  • Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!
  • Flexible Time Off Package - We offer a flexible annual leave policy plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
  • Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in USD) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
  • Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval.
  • Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
  • 401k - We offer a 401k plan and match up to 4%, with no minimum entry requirements and immediate vesting of employers’ contributions.

Our Interview Process

  • Talent Call (30 mins via Zoom)
    An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.
  • Panel Interview (60 mins via Zoom)
    A conversation with two of our Technical Directors focused on your approach to teamwork, client collaboration, and problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.
  • Technical Lead Assessment (90 mins via Zoom)
    A structured assessment led by a senior Technical Lead or Head of Engineering, designed to evaluate key aspects of a Technical Lead role. This session includes a selection of tasks to cover:

    Architecture Design - We want to see how you approach a high-level problem, demonstrating your design thinking and decision-making process.
    Technical Implementation - How do you turn a design into reality, taking into account business needs?
    Code Standards and Feedback - We want to see not just your own skills, but also how you improve those around you

There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

As part of our recruitment process, we conduct manual and electronic identity verification checks to confirm the identity of prospective employees.

Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence.

If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

Our salary range is $170,000 - 200,000 + bonus & benefits. Further details will be discussed in the initial interview, and final compensation will be determined based on skills, experience, and other job-related factors discussed during the interview process.

title: Junior Ubuntu Software Engineer
description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder led, profitable and growing. We are hiring junior engineers to work across the breadth of our Ubuntu Engineering organisation - engineers who care deeply for quality, performance and resilience in software, engineers who are just as comfortable designing and engineering new software as they are packaging, integrating, testing and shipping the incredible catalog of open source software provided by the Ubuntu repositories. Our engineers integrate the freshest open source software, provide robust upgrade paths and engineer the future of Ubuntu. Ubuntu is not just the world’s most deployed open source operating system, it's a platform that enables innovation for millions of users across the globe. Our community represents the full breadth of the developer experience; from students, hobbyists and freelancers to high performance engineering and creative teams in corporate and academic environments. The four key teams that ship Ubuntu are Foundations : maintaining foundational software: architectures, package managers, compilers, toolchains, bootloaders, filesystems and core utilities Server: leading the design, evolution and future of our Ubuntu Server distribution Desktop: driving Ubuntu Desktop, our future immutable desktop: Ubuntu Core Desktop, WSL, gaming technology, and a suite of modern applications for the desktop crafted with Flutter Debcrafters: a new team responsible for the forward movement, maintenance and overall health of the Ubuntu archive: one of the most abundant repositories of open source software available today Bring your existing expertise and learn new skills by working on one of the most prolific pieces of open source software. As an engineer working on Ubuntu you could work on any or all of the following categories: Development : design, build and ship new foundational systems software and applications in Rust, Go, Flutter, and Python Architecture : engineer the integration of open source from boot firmware to cloud applications deployment Packaging : a combination of Debian and Snap packaging to ship software in the distribution Automation : build and maintain the machinery responsible for building, testing and shipping Ubuntu Distro Engineering : the maintenance and evolution of a Linux distribution and its repositories If you have skills in those areas, or you have other skills you believe could contribute to Ubuntu, and you're keen to get started building your career in open source, then this is the role for you. Our junior career path caters for both new graduates and early careers engineers. At Canonical, you will have the opportunity to engage with and contribute to the broader open source community. We're looking for individuals who can help build a thriving community and contribute with enthusiasm and precision to a broad range of technologies. Location : We have remote roles open in every time zone. The role entails Based on the first round of interviews, we identify specific teams where you might be an excellent fit and conduct second-round interviews with those teams. Our engineers are: Designing, building and shipping software in Rust, Go, Python and C/C++ Packaging, integrating, testing and uploading open source software to the Ubuntu repositories Debugging issues, then designing and delivering robust solutions Authoring and improving technical and community documentation Contributing to upstream and neighboring open source projects Collaborating as part of a globally distributed team Continuously learning and progressing their technical and professional skills What we are looking for in you An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or STEM, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path Drive and a track record of going above and beyond expectations A passion for open source software Experience with Rust, Go, Python, Flutter or C/C++ Professional written and spoken English Excellent communication and interpersonal skills Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each Nice-to-have skills Familiarity with Linux distributions Familiarity with system debugging tools and techniques Familiarity with automation tooling and CI/CD systems Experience contributing to open source projects What we offer you We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical is an equal opportunity employer We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role. This position also requires traveling to client sites within the U.S. , with travel expenses covered by the company . About Nearform Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact. Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI. Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart. As part of our Engineering function, you will work closely with clients to translate complex business requirements into innovative digital products. Whether you are a Senior Engineer, Tech Lead, or DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate with distributed teams, leveraging cutting-edge technologies to build secure, high-performance applications. Our Nearform engineers are known for building high-quality, scalable solutions that solve real world problems. About the Senior Software Engineer role As a Senior Engineer at Nearform your main task will be designing & building applications using React and Python. However, as you’ll likely work on a variety of projects your responsibilities may also include: Supporting component design, development and maintenance and taking responsibility for personal technical quality standards within the project team. Assisting with defining structured practices, especially in source code management, building and deployment. Designing and implementing data storage solutions. Optimising performance in applications for maximum speed and scalability. Getting feedback from users and clients, and building solutions for them. Assisting with the analysis of client requirements. Working with and supporting Technical Leaders in project execution and timely delivery. Collaborating with client teams. What we are looking for in this person: Significant experience delivering at a Senior Engineer level. Our Seniors typically have at least 8 years of commercial experience. Deep knowledge and experience with the JavaScript/Typescript, which must include experience with React Experience with Python backend development Experience with AI-native development practices and tools. Understanding of AI and agentic workflows, with a drive to stay at the forefront of emerging LLM technologies. Practical experience of delivering in an agile environment. Practical experience and knowledge of developing real-world solutions. Deep understanding of versioning control tools - e.g. Git. Testing experience and familiarity with testing tools at all levels, unit, integration and end-to-end testing. Practical and real-world experience working with databases and cloud environments. Experience building software collaboratively using pull requests and code reviews Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Professional proficiency in English. Nice to have: Experience with AI application development and Agentic frameworks and platforms (e.g., LangGraph, Agentspace, etc.) Benefits & Perks: Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance. Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem! Flexible Time Off Package - We offer a flexible annual leave policy plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more. Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in USD) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join. Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval. Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team. 401k - We offer a 401k plan and match up to 4%, with no minimum entry requirements and immediate vesting of employers’ contributions. Our Interview Process Talent Call (30 mins via Zoom) An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment. Technical Assessment (1 hour via Zoom) A live coding challenge with one of our trained interviewers. You'll be asked to build a working solution to a problem via screen sharing, demonstrating your Python expertise, problem-solving ability, and coding best practices in a real-time environment. Hiring Manager Interview (45 mins via Zoom) A conversation with a Hiring Manager focused on your approach to teamwork, client collaboration, and problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join. There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project Ready to Join Us? If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning. As part of our recruitment process, we conduct manual and electronic identity verification checks to confirm the identity of prospective employees. Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence. If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help. Our salary range is $150,000 - 180,000 + bonus & benefits. Further details will be discussed in the initial interview, and final compensation will be determined based on skills, experience, and other job-related factors discussed during the interview process.

Work across the full Linux stack from kernel through GUI to optimise Ubuntu, the world’s most widely used Linux desktop and server, for the latest silicon.

The role is a fast-paced, problem-solving role that’s challenging yet very exciting. The right candidate must be resourceful, articulate, and able to deliver on a wide variety of solutions across PC and IoT technologies. Our teams partner with specialist engineers from major silicon companies to integrate next-generation features and performance enhancements for upcoming hardware.

Location: This is a Globally remote role

What your day will look like

  • Design and implement the best Ubuntu integration for the latest IoT and server-class hardware platforms and software stacks
  • Work with partners to deliver a delightful, optimised, first class Ubuntu experience on their platforms
  • Take a holistic approach to the Ubuntu experience on partner platforms with inputs on technical plans, testing strategy, quality metrics
  • Participate as technical lead on complex customer engagements involving complete system architectures from cloud to edge
  • Help our customers integrate their apps, SDKs, build device OS images, optimize applications with Ubuntu Core, Desktop and Server
  • Work with the most advanced operating systems and application technologies available in the enterprise world.

Joining Canonical, you will partner with bright minds from all over the world, and work with an exciting set of new technologies in a fast growing company with a truly unique and ambitious vision to build a better platform with free software. You will work with customers on exciting IoT and server platforms and technologies, built to support different verticals: from robots to data centers, from telco to retail.

What we are looking for in you

  • You love technology and working with brilliant people
  • You have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, STEM or similar
  • You have experience with Linux packaging (Debian, RPM, Yocto)
  • You have experience working with open source communities and licences
  • You have experience working with C, C++
  • You can work in a globally distributed team through self-discipline and self-motivation.

Additional skills that you might also bring

  • Experience with graphics stacks
  • Good understanding of networking - TCP/IP, DHCP, HTTP/REST
  • Basic understanding of security best practices in IoT or server environments
  • Good communication skills, ideally public speaking experience
  • IoT / Embedded experience – from board and SoC, BMCs, bootloaders and firmware to OS, through apps and services
  • Some experience with Docker/OCI containers/K8s

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce.

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

  • Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!
  • Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Parental Leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’
  • Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

About us

The rapid transition to electric vehicles (EVs) is the biggest change in transportation since the Model T. Flipturn is building the EV charging and energy platform for the next generation of sustainable transportation. We're already working with the largest forward-thinking Fortune 500 EV fleets across trucking, transit, and autonomous.

Flipturn is now a part of Einride, a global company revolutionizing transportation by showing the world a new way to move, based on the latest digital, electric and autonomous technologies. Through a suite of EV charging and fleet solutions and freight capacity as a service operations, Einride enables businesses around the world to accelerate towards their sustainability goals. Einride’s customers include some of the world’s biggest shippers, including Fortune 500 companies.

At Flipturn, you’ll:

  • Build a climate/sustainability-focused product, working on projects that directly impact real-life EV infrastructure

  • Collaborate with a team of extremely talented and mission-driven teammates (Stripe, Samsara, Google, MIT, UC Berkeley)

  • Work with modern technologies and best in class tools (ex: Yocto, TypeScript, GraphQL, AWS, Cursor, Claude)

  • Build for the long term as part of Einride, a global leader in EV and autonomous transportation technology

The role

This role is focused on the Flipturn Controller, a cutting-edge onsite control computer that integrates with EV chargers, batteries, generators, meters, and utility programs. You'll be involved in building major features, getting feedback from customers, driving the vision of our EV charging platform, and setting the culture of our engineering team.

You'll work on projects like:

  • Integrating EV charging with on-site batteries and generators, utility programs, and other sources of control

  • Upgrading our embedded Linux systems, including build tooling (Yocto or similar), bootloaders, and board bring-up

  • Firmware and full-stack improvements to Flipturn's innovative energy management platform, for example helping customers participate in PG&E's Flex Connect program to get their sites up and running faster

We're looking for people who have:

  • 4-7 years of experience in software engineering

  • 2+ years of experience with firmware development

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems – build tooling (Yocto or similar), bootloaders, and board bring-up

  • Interest in working on firmware/hardware projects as well as full-stack product development, as needed to deliver a fully working end-to-end product

  • Experience on a fast-moving industry-leading technology team and delivering products and features end-to-end

  • Interest in using AI tools to accelerate software development

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: The anticipated range for this position is $190,000 - $230,000 base salary per year, with an additional equity component

  • Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans, including PPO and HSA options.

  • Retirement savings: 401(k) plan with an employer match.

  • Generous time off: 25 days of Paid Time Off (PTO). 15 paid sick days and 15 paid US holidays observed.

  • Wellness allowance: To support your personal well-being.

  • Offices in NYC and Austin, as well as regular team bonding weeks with remote team members
