title: Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer CCS – Europäische Standardisierung EU-Rail (50%)
description: Im Rahmen des europäischen Projekts «Europäische Standardisierung CCS-Strecke» arbeiten gemeinsam mit führenden internationalen Bahnindustrieunternehmen wie Siemens, Hitachi, Alstom und CAF sowie europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern wie DB, SNCF, RFI, ÖBB, Network Rail und ProRail an der Weiterentwicklung und Harmonisierung zukünftiger Bahnsysteme. Das Projekt ist Teil des Europe’s Rail Joint Undertaking (ERJU) und umfasst den System Pillar sowie den Innovation Pillar. Ziel ist die Entwicklung europaweit einheitlicher Betriebsprozesse, Systemarchitekturen und technischer Spezifikationen für die zukünftigen ERTMS-Zielsysteme, insbesondere ETCS Level 2 und Automatic Train Operation (ATO GoA 1/2). Die erarbeiteten Standards bilden die Grundlage für zukünftige europäische Betriebsvorschriften sowie für die Weiterentwicklung und Beschaffung von Sicherungsanlagen. Zur Unterstützung der internationalen Projektarbeiten suchen wir eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit als Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer im Bereich Control, Command and Signalling (CCS). System Engineering: Erarbeitung und Weiterentwicklung von Systemdefinitionen, Systemarchitekturen und technischen Systemspezifikationen im sicherheitsrelevanten Bahnumfeld (CCS). Spezifikationserstellung: Entwicklung und Abstimmung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen unter Berücksichtigung der Gesamtarchitektur sowie zukünftiger Bahnprozesse. Prozesskoordination: Verantwortung für die effiziente Umsetzung und kontinuierliche Optimierung der Arbeitsprozesse (Workstations) zur Erstellung der Systemspezifikationen. Operative Projektunterstützung: Unterstützung bei der Organisation, Koordination und Umsetzung der internationalen Arbeitsorganisation. Qualitätssicherung: Sicherstellung einer konsistenten, vollständigen und qualitativ hochwertigen Integration der Arbeitsergebnisse in die übergeordneten Systemspezifikationen. Stakeholder-Management: Zusammenarbeit und Abstimmung mit internationalen Industriepartnern, europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern sowie internen und externen Fachspezialisten. Standardisierung: Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung europäisch harmonisierter Betriebsprozesse und technischer Standards für zukünftige ERTMS-Systeme. Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (ETH, Universität oder Fachhochschule) in Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einem verwandten naturwissenschaftlichen Fachgebiet. Umfassende Kenntnisse des Bahnsystems, insbesondere des Bahnbetriebs und der Zugsteuerung. Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Bereich internationale Standardisierung im Bahnumfeld. Fundierte Erfahrung in der Erstellung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen im europäischen Umfeld. Erfahrung mit Application Lifecycle Management Tools, insbesondere Polarion. Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Inhalte verständlich und zielgruppengerecht zu vermitteln. Sicheres Auftreten im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen nationalen und internationalen Stakeholdern. Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. description: Was wir suchen Eine Person, die ihre Freunde als „technisch-affinen Menschenfreund“ beschreiben würden, und Lust darauf hat zu erklären und zu beraten. Aufgaben Kickoff: Du führst Kickoff-Calls per Video mit neuen Kunden und klärst, wie die Prozesse, die wir für sie automatisieren aussehen. Setup: Du richtest KI-Systeme nach unserem festen, dokumentierten Standard ein und verbindest ihn mit den Plattformen des Kunden, zum Beispiel Mail, Kalender und etc. Onboarding: Du begleitest den Kunden, bis alles rund läuft – mit Onboarding-Call und einer Woche Feedback-Runde. Support: Du betreust unsere bestehenden Kunden und antwortest innerhalb von 24 Stunden. Einen Großteil der Anfragen erledigt unsere KI, du kümmerst dich um den Rest. Kundenbeziehung: Du schreibst mit den Kunden, beantwortest Fragen und sorgst dafür, dass sie zufrieden sind 🤝 Produkt: Du sammelst Fehler und Kundenfeedback und gehst sie einmal pro Woche mit unserem Team durch, und wirkst aktiv an der Verbesserung unserer Produkte mit. Tempo: Nach der Einarbeitung betreust du mehrere Setups parallel und startest bis zu einen neuen Kunden pro Tag. So arbeiten wir dich ein Woche 1: Du lernst unsere Abläufe, unser Studio und den Setup-Standard kennen und baust deinen eigenen KI-Agenten, falls du noch keinen hast (inkl. aller relevanten Schulungen). Woche 2: Du bist bei Kickoff-Calls und Setups unseres Technik-Teams dabei. Ab Woche 3: Du führst deinen ersten eigenen Kickoff, und hast einen Mentor an deiner Seite, der dich dabei unterstützt. Nach rund 4 Wochen: Du machst Calls, Setup und Support eigenständig und übernimmst nach und nach immer mehr Eigenverantwortung. Qualifikation Du magst Technik und Menschen gleichermaßen und hast ggf. selbst mit KI-Werkzeugen wie Claude Code, Codex oder eigenen Agenten gearbeitet. Du telefonierst gern und erklärst Technik so, dass dich ein Schreinermeister und ein Geschäftsführer gleichermaßen verstehen. Du arbeitest sorgfältig und verantwortungsbewusst, gerade mit Kundendaten. Du willst Gas geben, dazulernen und persönlich wachsen. Deutsch fließend in Wort und Schrift (C2), denn unsere Kunden sind deutsche Unternehmer. Englisch hilft bei Dokumentation und Tools, ist aber keine Bedingung. Optional: Du wohnst im Umkreis von Düsseldorf oder München (unsere Standorte) Welcher Abschluss dahintersteht, ist uns egal. title: Data Platform Manager
description: About the role As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week. You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver. At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive. What You'll Do Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people. Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do. Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source. Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business. Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence. Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge. Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question. Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake. Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us. Requirements What You’ll Need Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field. 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's. Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously. Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does. Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams. Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope. Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there. Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases. Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI. Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus. Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it. Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up. Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus. Who You Are You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head. You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it. You enjoy growing engineers, and you understand that leading a small team means doing the work alongside them. Above all, you want to build something durable — a foundation that holds while the company scales on top of it. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Production & Quality)
description: About the role Behind every well-run plant is a shared understanding of how it is performing — and that understanding has to be built. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Production & Quality at Destinus, you are the bridge between the people who run our plants and the data that describes them. Plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers own the processes; our lakehouse holds the data those processes create. Your job is to connect the two, so that every production and quality figure, from the shopfloor to the leadership team, is defined by the business, built on the lakehouse, and trusted by both. This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what the business needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the production and quality data in the lakehouse and turning it into the reporting used across three European plants, including our Digital Shopfloor Management Solution, relied on by more than 300 people. You will also go to where the data is created and make it better there — improving how it is captured, automating what is still manual, and helping three plants work to one standard. At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our operations span multiple plants and teams, and your work will directly support the reliability, efficiency, and excellence required for mission-critical production. Join us in shaping the next era of aerospace operations. What You'll do Be the go-to contact between the business owners of production and quality data — plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on. Own the production and quality portfolio end to end: define the KPI, improve the process behind it, build the dashboard, and stand behind the number. Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head. Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it. Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed. Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets. Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first. Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines. Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction. Requirements What You’ll Need Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field. Experience in a production or quality environment; aerospace or another regulated industry is highly preferred. Solid understanding of manufacturing and quality metrics — throughput, cycle time, OEE, scrap and rework, first-pass yield — and of quality processes such as non-conformance handling, customer complaints and field returns, root cause analysis, and corrective actions. Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills. Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back. Able to explain data to non-technical colleagues and business needs to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition. Knowledge of ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, and familiarity with shopfloor or MES systems. A track record of improving or automating a process, not only reporting on it. Exposure to continuous improvement methods is a plus. Comfortable working across multiple sites and collaborating with production teams, quality engineers, and leadership alike. Fluent in English; Spanish, German or Dutch is a strong plus given our plant locations. Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred. Who You Are You are equally comfortable on a shopfloor and in a data model, and you speak both languages — the plant's and the lakehouse's. You know that the fastest way to fix a reporting problem is often to walk to the place where the data is created and ask how it gets entered — and then change it. You are structured and persistent, because aligning three plants on one way of working takes more than a good spreadsheet; it takes patience and conversations. You enjoy the detail of a root cause but stay focused on whether performance actually improved, and when something is manual or repetitive you would rather automate it than live with it. You turn numbers into stories, stories into priorities, and priorities into measurable change. Above all, you take ownership, challenge assumptions, and stay committed to operational excellence.   • Own the production and quality portfolio end to end: define the KPI, improve the process behind it, build the dashboard, and stand behind the number.
  • Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it.
  • Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed.
  • Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets.
  • Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines.
  • Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field.
  • Experience in a production or quality environment; aerospace or another regulated industry is highly preferred.

Who You Are

You are equally comfortable on a shopfloor and in a data model, and you speak both languages — the plant's and the lakehouse's. You know that the fastest way to fix a reporting problem is often to walk to the place where the data is created and ask how it gets entered — and then change it.

You are structured and persistent, because aligning three plants on one way of working takes more than a good spreadsheet; it takes patience and conversations. title: Senior Product Marketing Manager (m/w/d)
description: Die Energiewirtschaft steckt mitten in der größten Transition ihrer Geschichte. Energieversorger, Netzbetreiber und Lösungsanbieter brauchen Software, die da mithält, und sie brauchen jemanden, der ihnen klar und glaubwürdig erklärt, warum epilot genau die richtige Plattform ist. Als Senior Product Marketing Manager bist du genau diese Stimme im Markt. Du gestaltest mit, wie wir epilot als zentrale, AI-native Plattform für die neue Energiewelt positionieren. Und du sorgst dafür, dass Marketing, Sales und Customer Success eine gemeinsame Geschichte erzählen. Product Marketing ist für dich das Fundament jeder Kommunikation und nicht nur der Lieferant für Slides und Battle Cards? Dann lies weiter. epilot ist das XRM für die Energiewirtschaft: Unsere Plattform verbindet nicht nur Kund:innen, sondern auch Partner, Installateure, Lieferanten und interne Teams. Über 200 Energieversorger und Netzbetreiber arbeiten bereits damit, und unser Team aus über 120 Menschen wächst weiter. Wenn du Teil dieser Journey sein und epilot an entscheidender Stelle voranbringen möchtest, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung! Das erwartet dich Positionierung und Messaging der epilot Plattform liegen in deiner Verantwortung, für Energieversorger, Netzbetreiber und Lösungsanbieter. Produktfunktionen übersetzt du in Mehrwerte, die bei allen wichtigen Personas ankommen. Nah am Markt: In Sales-Calls, im Gespräch mit Kund:innen und auf Branchenevents erfährst du, was Energieversorger gerade umtreibt. Daraus hältst du ICPs, Personas und Wettbewerbsanalysen aktuell und machst sie zu Wissen, mit dem das ganze Unternehmen arbeitet. Produktkampagnen und Markteinführungen steuerst du inhaltlich, von der Story bis zu den Kernbotschaften, gemeinsam mit unserem Campaign & Growth Marketing. Auch die inhaltliche Qualität unserer Produktseiten und weitere produktnahe Inhalte liegt in deiner Verantwortung. Sales und Customer Success machst du sprechfähig: mit Pitch-Materialien, Argumentationshilfen, Einwandbehandlung und Trainings. AI-gestützte Workflows für Product Marketing baust du auf und entwickelst sie weiter, etwa für Persona- und Wettbewerbsanalysen, Messaging oder Sales-Materialien. AI ist für dich kein Knopfdruck: Die Logik dahinter entwickelst du selbst. Unsere Junior Product Marketing Managerin führst du fachlich und begleitest sie in ihrer Entwicklung. Strategy, Produktmanagement, Sales, Customer Success, Campaign & Growth sowie Event Marketing schätzen dich als Sparringspartner:in. Das bringst du mit Mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Marketing , idealerweise im Product Marketing. Positionierung und Messaging hast du schon selbst verantwortet. Komplexe Produkte verstehst du schnell und erklärst sie einfach. Dabei findest du die Worte, bei denen Zielgruppen nicken, und nicht die, die nur intern gut klingen. Strategisch denken und selbst anpacken gehören für dich zusammen. Ein Messaging-Framework entwickelst du ebenso gern wie eine Produktseite oder einen Sales-Pitch. Auf ein Briefing wartest du nicht: Wo es eine klare Story braucht, bringst du sie auf den Weg. AI-Tools nutzt du nicht nur. Am liebsten baust du eigene Workflows, statt dich auf fertige Lösungen zu verlassen. Neugier auf die Energiewirtschaft ist entscheidend. Branchenerfahrung oder Wissen über Energieprozesse ist ein großes Plus, wichtiger ist aber deine Lust, tief einzutauchen. Überzeugungskraft: Stakeholder bis hin zum C-Level gewinnst du mit klaren Argumenten. Außerdem macht es dir Freude, andere fachlich zu begleiten und weiterzuentwickeln. Sprachen: Stilsicheres Deutsch auf C2-Niveau ist ein Muss, denn dein Messaging muss im deutschen Markt sitzen. Dazu sprichst du fließend Englisch, unsere Unternehmenssprache. Das bieten wir dir Flexibles Arbeiten: Remote arbeiten, wann immer es passt, und regelmäßig in Köln zusammenkommen, wenn persönlicher Austausch zählt. Die Möglichkeit, die erfolgreichste SaaS-Plattform auf dem Energiemarkt mit aufzubauen. Start-up-Mentalität: dynamische Atmosphäre und großartiger Teamspirit. Ein stark wachsendes Unternehmen mit offener Kommunikationskultur, motivierten Kolleg:innen, und internationaler Unternehmenskultur Exponentielle Lernkurve – epilot wächst rasant, selbiges erwarten wir von dir Einen zentralen und modernen Standort im Herzen von Köln mit coolen Cafés direkt um die Ecke Transparenz – Wir pflegen eine sehr flache und offene Unternehmenskultur, alles ist einsehbar und steht zur Diskussion. description: Warum wir tun, was wir tun Unsere Psyche ist das Fenster, durch das wir die Welt sehen – mal grau, mal hell. Wer lernt, dieses Fenster zu verstehen, kann jeden Tag eine neue Perspektive gewinnen. Aus psychischen Herausforderungen können Chancen zum Wachsen werden. Und weil Glück ansteckend ist, verändert sich so die Gesellschaft: one mind at a time. Warum es diese Rolle braucht Immer mehr Arbeitgebende und Versicherungen machen Aepsy für ihre Mitarbeitenden zugänglich – vom KMU bis zum Grossunternehmen. So erhalten mehr Menschen frühzeitig Zugang zu passender psychologischer Unterstützung. Doch ein Angebot allein reicht nicht. Mitarbeitende müssen Aepsy kennen, verstehen und ihm vertrauen. Sie müssen wissen, wie sie das Angebot nutzen können, wenn sie Unterstützung brauchen. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Partnerschaften echte Wirkung entsteht. Dafür entwickelst du Aktivierungsmassnahmen, koordinierst Projekte und arbeitest eng mit HR-Verantwortlichen sowie unseren Teams aus Sales, Marketing, Operations und Product zusammen. Was du bewegen wirst Partnerschaften gestalten: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen, baust langfristige Beziehungen auf und verstehst, was deine Ansprechpersonen bewegt. Menschen erreichen und aktivieren: Du entwickelst Kommunikations- und Aktivierungsmassnahmen, die Mitarbeitende auf Aepsy aufmerksam machen und zur Nutzung motivieren. Projekte ins Rollen bringen: Du planst und koordinierst Projekte von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung, behältst Deadlines im Blick und bringst alle Beteiligten zusammen. Wirkung sichtbar machen: Du analysierst Aktivierungs- und Nutzungszahlen und leitest daraus konkrete Verbesserungsmassnahmen ab. Dinge besser machen: Du hinterfragst Abläufe, bringst eigene Ideen ein und entwickelst unsere Partnerschaften, Prozesse und das Produkt weiter. Was du mitbringst Du musst nicht bereits alles können. Viel wichtiger ist uns, wie du denkst, wie du mit Menschen umgehst und was dich antreibt. Erste Berufserfahrung in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, HR oder einem verwandten Bereich. Einen Hintergrund in Psychologie oder Gesundheitsförderung ist ein Plus aber kein Muss. Freude am Aufbau von Beziehungen, Begeisterungsfähigkeit und ein ausgeprägtes Verantwortungsbewusstsein Selbstständige, strukturierte Arbeitsweise und die Fähigkeit, auch bei mehreren parallelen Projekten den Überblick zu behalten Analytisches Denken, Interesse an Zahlen und Freude daran, Prozesse zu hinterfragen und zu verbessern Freude an einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem nicht immer alles vorgegeben ist und Eigeninitiative gefragt ist Sehr gute Deutsch- sowie Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Bereitschaft, in einem 100-%-Pensum zu arbeiten und mehrheitlich vor Ort in unserem Büro im Herzen von Zürich tätig zu sein. Eine reine Remote-Tätigkeit ist nicht möglich. Was wir dir bieten Arbeit, die etwas bewirkt. Deine Arbeit hilft Menschen, psychologische Unterstützung zu finden, wenn sie sie brauchen. Du trägst dazu bei, mentale Gesundheit zugänglicher zu machen. Ein Team, das dich stärkt. Du arbeitest eng mit Sales, Marketing, Product und unserer Psycholog:innen-Community zusammen. raw.description:
Warum wir tun, was wir tun

Unsere Psyche ist das Fenster, durch das wir die Welt sehen – mal grau, mal hell. Wer lernt, dieses Fenster zu verstehen, kann jeden Tag eine neue Perspektive gewinnen. Aus psychischen Herausforderungen können Chancen zum Wachsen werden. Und weil Glück ansteckend ist, verändert sich so die Gesellschaft: one mind at a time.

Warum es diese Rolle braucht

Immer mehr Arbeitgebende und Versicherungen machen Aepsy für ihre Mitarbeitenden zugänglich – vom KMU bis zum Grossunternehmen. So erhalten mehr Menschen frühzeitig Zugang zu passender psychologischer Unterstützung.

Doch ein Angebot allein reicht nicht. Mitarbeitende müssen Aepsy kennen, verstehen und ihm vertrauen. Sie müssen wissen, wie sie das Angebot nutzen können, wenn sie Unterstützung brauchen.

Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Partnerschaften echte Wirkung entsteht. Dafür entwickelst du Aktivierungsmassnahmen, koordinierst Projekte und arbeitest eng mit HR-Verantwortlichen sowie unseren Teams aus Sales, Marketing, Operations und Product zusammen.

Was du bewegen wirst

  • Partnerschaften gestalten: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen, baust langfristige Beziehungen auf und verstehst, was deine Ansprechpersonen bewegt.

  • Projekte ins Rollen bringen: Du planst und koordinierst Projekte von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung, behältst Deadlines im Blick und bringst alle Beteiligten zusammen.

  • Wirkung sichtbar machen: Du analysierst Aktivierungs- und Nutzungszahlen und leitest daraus konkrete Verbesserungsmassnahmen ab.

  • Dinge besser machen: Du hinterfragst Abläufe, bringst eigene Ideen ein und entwickelst unsere Partnerschaften, Prozesse und das Produkt weiter.

Was du mitbringst

Du musst nicht bereits alles können. Viel wichtiger ist uns, wie du denkst, wie du mit Menschen umgehst und was dich antreibt.

  • Erste Berufserfahrung in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, HR oder einem verwandten Bereich. Einen Hintergrund in Psychologie oder Gesundheitsförderung ist ein Plus aber kein Muss.

raw.jobDescription:
Caylent is an AI-first cloud services company that helps organizations turn ambitious ideas into meaningful business impact. As an AWS Premier Tier Services Partner and a charter member of Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network, we combine deep expertise in AWS, artificial intelligence, and Anthropic’s Claude platform to help customers modernize their technology, build intelligent products, and move AI from experimentation into production.

Our capabilities span generative and agentic AI, cloud migration and modernization, cloud-native application development, data and analytics, DevOps, managed services, security and compliance, and customer experience transformation. At Caylent, our people always come first.

We are a fully remote global company with employees in Canada, the United States and Latin America. We celebrate the culture of each of our team members and foster a community of technological curiosity. Come talk to us to learn more about what it means to be a Caylien!

The Mission

This role is a Senior QA/Test Engineer specializing in Amazon Connect and contact center technology, responsible for designing and executing comprehensive test strategies across contact flows, routing, IVR/self-service, and AI-driven conversational agents. They validate legacy-to-Connect migrations, build and maintain manual and automated test suites (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium) spanning UI, API, and serverless backend components, and ensure production readiness through cutover validation, monitoring verification, and incident triage. Beyond hands-on testing, they partner with engineers to shift quality left, run UAT sessions with customer stakeholders, and contribute reusable test assets and mentorship to strengthen Caylent's contact center QA practice.

Your Assignment

Test Strategy & Contact Center Quality

  • Design and execute test strategies for Amazon Connect implementations covering contact flows, routing logic, IVR/self-service, Cases/Tasks workflows, and Contact Lens configurations
  • Build test plans that validate AI agent behavior: intent recognition accuracy, escalation paths, barge-in/fallback handling, hallucination guardrails, and multilingual/SSML voice interactions
  • Validate legacy-to-Connect migrations (i.e. Avaya, Genesys, Connect, NICE) through parallel-run testing, flow conversion verification, and data migration validation
  • Define and track quality metrics (defect density, test coverage, escape rate) and report on release readiness to delivery leads and customer stakeholders
  • Hands-on experience with web application and web automation testing

Manual, Automated & Full-Stack Testing

  • Build, maintain, and execute manual and automated IVR test suites, using tools such as Cyara, Hammer, or Botium (preferred).
  • Build, maintain, and execute manual and automated web application test suites, using frameworks such as Cypress, Selenium, or Playwright (preferred).
  • Build and maintain manual and automated test suites: Playwright E2E and API tests, Cypress, Selenium, integration tests against live Amazon Connect instances, and end-to-end tests of Amazon connect call flows.
  • Test custom Agent Workspace experiences (Amazon Connect, Agent Assist)
  • Validate serverless, event-driven backends (Lambda, EventBridge, Step Functions, SQS/SNS, DynamoDB, Kinesis) with integration and contract tests

Production Readiness & Operations

  • Execute phased rollout and cutover validation for live contact centers, where testing gaps translate directly into missed calls and customer impact
  • Verify monitoring and alerting coverage (CloudWatch metrics, alarms, dashboards) across voice, chat, tasks, queues, agents, Lambda, and AI agents prior to go-live
  • Participate in production incident triage, reproducing defects and validating fixes across the contact center stack
  • Perform security and compliance validation: least-privilege IAM checks, DevSecOps scan review, and encryption standard verification

Collaboration & Practice Contribution

  • Partner with engineers during development to shift testing left: pairing on test design, reviewing acceptance criteria, and flagging risk areas early
  • Run UAT sessions with customer stakeholders, triage findings, and drive defects to resolution ahead of production cutovers
  • Contribute reusable test assets (automated suites, test data sets, QA checklists) back to the CXE practice
  • Mentor junior QA engineers on contact center testing patterns and Caylent's quality standards

Your Qualifications

  • 8+ years of QA/test engineering experience, including 3+ years testing contact center, CCaaS, or IVR/voice platforms
  • Hands-on experience with Amazon Connect or a comparable CCaaS platform: contact flows, routing, Cases/Tasks, and reporting
  • Proficiency with automated testing frameworks (Playwright E2E and API tests, Cypress, Selenium) for unit, integration, and E2E testing
  • Experience testing serverless/event-driven AWS architectures (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Step Functions)
  • Working knowledge of conversational AI / voice testing considerations: intent accuracy, latency, fallback behavior
  • Strong defect documentation and triage skills; comfortable running UAT sessions with business and technical stakeholders
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) and integrating automated tests into deployment workflows

Preferred Qualifications

  • Contact center migration testing experience (i.e. Avaya, Genesys, Connect, NICE)
  • Experience with AI observability/trace validation (agent spans, token/cost attribution) or accessibility engineering
  • AWS certifications (Solutions Architect, Developer, or ML/Connect-relevant Specialty)
  • Contact center operations fluency: Quality management, outbound compliance, and CX KPIs
  • Consulting or client-delivery background
  • Hands on experience with Cyara Botium

Benefits

  • 100% remote work
  • Medical Insurance for you and eligible dependents
  • Generous holidays and flexible PTO
  • Competitive phantom equity
  • Paid for exams and certifications
  • Peer bonus awards
  • State of the art laptop and tools
  • Equipment & Office Stipend
  • Individual professional development plan
  • Annual stipend for Learning and Development
  • Work with an amazing worldwide team and in an incredible corporate culture

raw.jobDescription:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is building the next generation of industrial robots -- hardware that's powerful, affordable, and designed to scale. We're the largest U.S. industrial robotics company by robots shipped, and our robots are showing up on factory floors everywhere from independent machine shops to NASA and Lockheed Martin.

Note: This role is technically remote, but you must live on the west coast (preference for California). This job is customer-facing and requires up to 50% domestic travel, Monday through Friday. If that makes you nervous, this probably isn't the right fit. If that sounds like a perk, read on.

Also note: This is not a software engineering role. If you're looking for a job where you sit at a desk and write application code, this is the wrong job description. If you want to actually build things, wire things up, and watch them run -- keep reading.

The Role

The Senior Applications Engineer is one of the rarest profiles in industrial automation -- and one of the most important roles at Standard Bots.

You're not a mechanical engineer. You're not an electrical engineer. You're not a software engineer. You're all three, and you know how to make them talk to each other. You can look at a customer's production line, understand what's broken or slow or manual, and figure out how to fix it with a robot. Then you build the proof of concept, get on a plane, and go install it.

From pre to post sale, you're the one working closely with the sales team to make the solution real. You'll build the proof of concept, design the integration, write the python scripts, build the fixture, run the wiring, and commission the cell -- then train the customer's team on how to use it. You'll also help run demos at trade shows, support trainings at customer sites and in our shop, and be the technical backbone for every customer engagement that requires hands-on expertise.

This is a builder's role. Tinkerers welcome. People who get bored at a desk are strongly encouraged to apply.

What You'll Do

Solution Design & Proof of Concept

- Work with the sales team and customers to understand automation goals, production constraints, and integration requirements

- Design practical, buildable solutions around Standard Bots' hardware -- and build the proof of concept yourself to validate it works before anyone signs anything

- Develop application notes, sample code, and supporting documentation that help customers and internal teams understand how to replicate and scale solutions

Field Installation & Integration

- Travel to customer sites to install, program, wire, and commission robotic cells

- Own the integration from mechanical setup through software configuration -- fixtures, I/O, PLC handshakes, safety, test, sign-off

- Troubleshoot on-site when things don't go as planned (and sometimes they don't) -- you stay until it works

Customer Training & Support

- Train customer operators and technicians on Standard Bots hardware and software -- both on-site and at our facility

- Support customers post-install as they find new applications and push the limits of what the robot can do

- Be a trusted technical resource for the accounts you've worked with -- they'll call you when something comes up

Trade Shows & Demos

- Represent Standard Bots at industry events and trade shows -- build the demo, run it live, talk shop with engineers and plant managers on the floor

- Help develop and maintain demo systems that show the breadth of what Standard Bots hardware can do

Internal Collaboration

- Feed real-world integration learnings back to our hardware and software engineering teams -- you're on the front lines and your input shapes the product

- Assist in-house engineering with testing new features, peripherals, and integrations as we expand the platform

What We're Looking For

- A genuine trifecta: you're comfortable with mechanical systems, electrical systems, and software -- not just one of the three

- 6+ years of hands-on experience with industrial automation fundamentals: PLC programming and ladder logic, pneumatics, DC power systems (you know the difference between NPN and PNP), robot programming (any platform), and Python scripting

- Proficiency with CAD -- SolidWorks preferred, but we care more that you can design and think in 3D than which tool you use

- Customer-facing experience -- you can explain a technical integration to an engineer, a plant manager, and an ops director in the same conversation and land differently with each one

- A genuine bias for getting things done in the field, not just in theory -- you'd rather build it than write about it

- Comfort with up to 50% domestic travel; this role is hands-on and on-site by nature

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline -- or equivalent hands-on experience that tells the same story

Nice to Have

- Prior experience with collaborative robots (UR, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, or similar)

- Familiarity with machine tending, palletizing, welding, or assembly automation applications

- Experience with vision systems, force/torque sensing, or custom end-of-arm tooling

- Background in a manufacturing or production environment -- you've worked on or near a factory floor before

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $150,000 to $200,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: CDI - Senior Product Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

 

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

 

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

 

Rémunération : 60 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 6 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

You will be responsible for generating leads, establishing partnerships and alliances that support our business objectives, and growing the number of chargeable expanded access programs (named patient sales) we run for our partners.

  3. Set the bar. Author specs, run the spec-driven workflow, and stand up the eval and review gates that make agent-authored code trustworthy.

  4. Harvest the field. Turn recurring customer patterns into platform capabilities, so learning compounds instead of fragmenting into bespoke forks.

  5. Lead by example. Write the load-bearing code, pair with your engineers, raise their craft, and grow the squad as the leverage you ship earns it.

Your impact

Every Solution squad and every customer deployment is only as strong as the platform underneath it. Own a capability cluster well and you create leverage the entire company compounds on — the difference between a platform that scales and a pile of one-off forks.

  • AI-native ways of working (agentic workflows, eval harnesses, spec-driven development)

Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.

This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.

About the Role

Pelico's customers feel one pain above all: missing parts that block delivery. The Solution squads are where we turn Pelico's platform into a product that fixes it. Each squad owns one solution surface — Material Coverage & inventory, Quality, Supplier & customer Collaboration / AI Buyer, MRO & Aftermarket, Program Management, or Strategic Account Support — composing our platform's building blocks into workflows that work across many customers. You'll lead one surface end to end: ship it fast, keep it configuration-first, and feed real customer patterns back into the platform — while our Regional Solution Engineering pods carry the day-to-day customer relationship.

What You'll Do

You'll own a solution surface — and build it yourself:

  • Ship the surface. Compose configuration, compute, widgets, connectors, and agents into customer-facing workflows that pass a real acid test on real customers.

  • Stay configuration-first. Solve in Phoenix YAML wherever you can, reach for code only when it's worth it, and never let the surface fragment into per-customer forks.

  • Set the bar. Author specs, run the spec-driven workflow, and put eval and review gates on anything AI-assisted that touches a customer.

  • Harvest the field. Spot the patterns that recur across accounts and turn them into platform capabilities, so the next customer is faster.

  • Lead by example. Write the code, pair with your squad and the engineers deploying at customer sites, raise the bar, and grow the team as the impact you ship earns it.

Your impact: Customers buy outcomes — shortages caught, deliveries recovered, quality exceptions resolved. Your squad is where the platform becomes those outcomes. Own a surface well and you make Pelico's revenue engine both faster and more defensible — and you keep it from collapsing into bespoke work that can't scale.

About You

This is a lead-by-example role for a senior full-stack engineer with real product and customer judgment. You're energized by shipping outcomes under real constraints, you decide what not to build, and you lead by being in the code with your team.

You'll need:

  • A track record of shipping customer-facing product software end to end, full-stack, under real delivery pressure

  • Strong, current hands-on coding — we build in Kotlin / Java 25 (backend) and TypeScript / React (frontend); strong in one and credible across, or a fast learner

  • Product and customer judgment — scope to outcomes, cut to MVP under deadline, decide what not to build

  • A configuration-first, anti-bespoke instinct — you build for many customers, not one fork at a time

  • A track record of leading engineers by example, not by leaving the keyboard

  • You actively embrace AI tools as part of how you work — curious about what's possible and quick to adopt new ways of working smarter and faster.

  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted workflows — whether for writing, research, analysis, coding, or productivity — and a genuine interest in staying at the frontier of what these tools can do.

Nice to have:

  • Aerospace / defense / supply-chain / discrete-manufacturing context (MRP, BoM, coverage, MRO/TAT, program management, procurement)

  • Forward-deployed / solutions-engineering / customer-embedded experience, feeding learnings back into a platform

  • Configuration- or low-code-driven product experience (YAML/DSL, composable UI, workflow authoring)

  • AI-native ways of working (agentic workflows, eval on AI output, spec-driven development)

  • French is a plus, not a requirement

If you bring the essentials and a strong mix of the rest, we want to hear from you — we're hiring the person who'll make this real, not a checklist.

Why Pelico

We're building something genuinely hard and genuinely important. Here's what that comes with:

  • Meaningful equity — you're building this with us, so you'll own a piece of it

  • Competitive salary benchmarked to your market

  • Flexible, hybrid work model — we care about output, not face time

  • Learning & development budget — we invest in people who invest in themselves

  • Opportunity to work with some of the world's most complex and fascinating manufacturing operations

  • A team that takes the work seriously without taking themselves too seriously

  • Work at the frontier of applied AI, with exposure to cutting-edge AI tooling and operational challenges inside a high-growth startup

We move fast and we're transparent at every step.

Hey there!
We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Behind the user-friendly iOS and Android apps and webpage that work across the world is the engineering team. We are in charge of creating, developing, improving, and maintaining all Fever services so that more people can have an amazing experience.

About the role

Location: Spain - 100% Home office friendly

What are we looking for:

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Engineering team with outstanding software development talent proven by great work results/experience. Somebody who cares about code quality and not just getting things done, but getting things done right.

If you're smart, have great energy, can't think about a system without a CI/CD pipeline, and you want to thrive in a fast-paced environment, we are in sync.

What would you do at Fever?

During your first month at Fever (Onboarding period):

  • You’ll join a structured onboarding program designed to help you ramp up smoothly. During this period, you will:
  • Meet your buddy and team, and get to know Fever’s culture and ways of working.
  • Set up your local environment and become familiar with our Python-based stack, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Learn about our architecture and observability tools while contributing small improvements and fixes.
  • Have your first code running in production and a clear understanding of our delivery flow and processes.
  • By the end of the onboarding, you’ll be ready to join your long-term squad and start contributing to larger initiatives.

After 3 months at Fever:

  • You’ll be confidently collaborating and delivering at full speed. You will:
  • Design and implement end-to-end features within your squad.
  • Participate in architectural discussions and propose improvements across our services and APIs.
  • Work with event-driven systems and focus on performance, reliability, and scalability.
  • Collaborate closely with Product, Data, and other Engineering teams to enhance our platform and developer experience.

By your 6th month at Fever:

  • You’ll be fully established as a key contributor in your team. You will:
  • Take ownership of core components and help evolve their architecture.
  • Lead by example through code reviews, design sessions, and mentoring.
  • Contribute to best practices in areas like scalability, observability, and system design.
  • Drive continuous improvement and have a visible impact on how we build high-performing services at scale.
  • Become an expert in your domain, using business context and technical excellence to drive strategic initiatives forward

About you

Must have skills:

  • Strong knowledge of best practices, testing, and design patterns
  • You are proficient in business English
  • You know how to deliver code from development to production
  • Experience with RESTful APIs (implementation and consumption)
  • Knowledge of relational databases and SQL
  • Experience with event streaming platforms such as Kafka or RabbitMQ
  • Handling services with high concurrencies and high volume requests.

We use these technologies, so it would be a plus if you have experience in:

  • Django/Flask
  • PostgreSQL and Redis
  • AWS, Docker, and Kubernetes

Benefits & Perks

  • 23 days of vacation plus half a day on your birthday
  • Private medical insurance sponsored by the company
  • 40% discount on Fever Marketplace
  • Flexibility to work from home
  • English & Spanish conversational classes
  • Wellhub (former Gympass) membership
  • Possibility to receive part of your salary in advance with Payflow
  • Flexible remuneration with Cobee
  • Budget for engineering events and trainings
  • Young and international environment
  • Attractive compensation package consisting of base salary and the potential to earn a significant bonus for top performance.
    • Base Salary: 50K - 75K EUR
    • Total Compensation: 67K - 90K EUR (Including Base, Variable, and Stock Options)

About the process

Fever aims to provide the best and fastest possible experience to our candidates. This is how it would look like:

  • Talent Interview - 1h: An intro to Fever, our culture and a conversation about your background and experience.
  • Technical Interview - 2h: A deep dive into your technical expertise through a system design discussion and a short coding exercise, giving you the chance to walk us through your reasoning and problem-solving approach — and ask us anything about your day-to-day at Fever.
  • Manager Interview - 1.5h: A conversation about how you communicate context and trade-offs, own outcomes, quantify impact, and think about reliability, scale, and system design decisions.

raw.jobDescription:
About Neuroscale

Neuroscale is on a mission to fill the world’s most important roles.

Recruiting is a zero-sum game. The best people get hired once, and the teams that move fastest win. We build Arbi, an AI recruiting platform that combines autonomous agents with elite recruiters so world-class companies and federal agencies can hire well and grow fast.

Arbi searches 800M+ profiles, runs outreach, and interviews candidates at scale. Through every search, placement, and interaction on our platform, we capture proprietary hiring data that no one else has at scale, and that data powers the agentic systems we are building to make hiring faster, smarter, and more precise.

We believe AI will create more jobs, not less. As companies move faster with fewer constraints, they will hire more ambitiously and for roles that did not exist before, making the hiring layer more critical than ever.

We hold a USAF SBIR Direct-to-Phase-II contract, sell into federal through Carahsoft, and work with enterprise, federal, and regulated organizations that most AI startups cannot touch. Our second product, Athena, extends the same agent infrastructure into federal agency workflows.

We are a small, founder-led team and this is one of the first engineering seats.

About the Role

You will work directly with the founders on the hardest technical questions in the product:

  • How do we understand the nuance in a hiring requirement well enough to find the person a filter & criteria search never would?

  • How do we interview candidates at scale and turn those conversations into a data edge no public profile can give you?

  • How do agents decide who to reach out to, what to say, and when to hand off to a human?

  • How do we make a recruiter say “wow” in the first five minutes?

You will design, build, and ship features end to end, most of them built on LLMs. Recent work includes agent execution infrastructure, feedback loops that improve search quality from recruiter behavior, and multi-tenant deployment for regulated customers.

Our stack: Next.js + React, Node.js, Python FastAPI, OpenSearch (Elasticsearch), Temporal, and a range of inference providers and models.

About You

  • You have built something from scratch. A startup, a product, a system people depend on.

  • You ship. We care more about what you have built than where you have worked.

  • You are high agency. You find the highest-leverage problem, decide it is yours, and attack it.

  • You have shown excellence somewhere: work, school, open source, a side project that took off.

  • You take asymmetric bets. Joining a founding team is one of them.

  • You have real experience with the core of our stack: Next.js, Node.js, AWS, and search or data infrastructure.

  • Experience with LLM products, voice or conversational AI, or search at scale is a plus, not a filter.

  • Based in or willing to relocate to Northern Virginia. We build in person.

Why Founding

  • Direct ownership of core systems from day one. Your decisions become the architecture.

  • Meaningful founding equity. You should share in what you build.

  • Work on problems with real stakes: federal hiring, regulated industries, roles that matter.

  • A front-row seat to going from early traction to category leader.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitve salary plus meaningful founding equity.

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Meals provided in office.

  • Relocation support for the right candidate.

Neuroscale AI is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Senior Software Developer, Search
description: MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform for industrial and frontline teams. More than 15,000 customers , including McDonalds, Michaels, Cintas, Redimix, and U.S. LBM, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 16 million managed assets and 92 million completed work orders. In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining Autodesk Operations Solutions , the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations. Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours. About the Role We’re starting a new Search team to make it easier for users find exactly what they need across MaintainX. You’ll play a critical role in designing, building, and scaling search infrastructure that reflects the unique shape of the MaintainX domain. This is a zero-to-one role. You’ll be scoping ambiguity, shipping usable search early, and evolving it with fast feedback loops. If you enjoy building systems from scratch, obsess over performance and relevance, and want your work to power daily decisions across industries, we’d love to talk. What You'll Do: Design and build MaintainX’s end-to-end search and retrieval platform — from indexing pipelines and ranking systems to AI-facing query layers. Partner with product and domain experts to model search across core entities like work orders, assets, and procedures, ensuring high-relevance results. Ship fast, iterate fast, launch early versions, gather feedback, and improve rapidly. Operate and optimize distributed systems, ensuring reliability, performance, and scalability under real-world load. Drive architectural decisions, balancing correctness, performance, and long-term maintainability. Own integrations between search systems and upstream data sources. Explore semantic search, vector retrieval, and AI-enhanced relevance using modern ML tooling. On-call duties (currently business hours) About You: Hands-on experience designing, building, and operating production-grade search systems end-to-end — including indexing, query execution, relevance tuning, and infrastructure — using technologies such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Lucene, Solr, or similar. Understanding of embeddings, chunking, and retrieval strategies. Familiarity with search-specific tuning: analyzers, BM25, shard sizing, cluster health, and relevance optimization. Comfort taking systems from implementation to deployment and production operation, working across backend services, data pipelines, and integration points as needed. An expert level of English, both spoken and written, is required, as the individual will need to lead platform engineering managers across multiple teams, present technical priorities to executive stakeholders, and align with engineering leaders outside Québec on a daily basis. Nice to Have: Experience evaluating and improving search relevance using both qualitative analysis and quantitative metrics. Experience shipping AI-powered or LLM-integrated backend systems Comfortable using modern AI tools like GPT, Copilot, or Cursor to boost productivity and streamline development. Understanding of multi-tenancy and data security , including ACLs, field-level access controls, and secure index partitioning. Experience building observability and success metrics into systems to monitor performance, usage, and impact. Our mission is to keep the physical world running. Factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses stay up because the people who maintain them have tools worth using. That is what we build. Compensation and benefits. Base pay is one part of the package. Depending on the role, compensation may also include commission, an annual bonus and equity. Benefits differ by country. For roles in the United States, Autodesk’s benefits are described at benefits.autodesk.com . For roles in Canada and other countries, the plan differs on health coverage, retirement and leave, and your recruiter will walk you through it. Belonging. We take pride in a culture where everyone can thrive. More at autodesk.com/company/global-belonging . More on where this is going: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost on building the future of connected operations , and AOS SVP Stephen Hooper on welcoming MaintainX to Autodesk .

We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting.

  • Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments.

  • Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan.

  • Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation.

  • Bring global flood models to the local scale

  • Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally.

  • Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation.

  • Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs.

  • Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models.

  • Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance.

  • Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers.

  • Stay close to the real world

  • We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand.

  • You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions.

  • You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use.

  • You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers.

  • You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information.

  • You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment.

  • You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations.

title: Senior Supply Chain Operations Manager- Factor Europe (all genders)
description:
The role

Factor is our newest brand - a healthy, ready-to-eat meal delivery service, and one of the fastest-growing parts of the HelloFresh Group’s European business. 

We're looking for a Senior Supply Chain Operations Manager (alle genders) to lead our Procurement Operations function and ensure our supply chain is running efficiently, scalable, and commercially effective. You'll oversee the end-to-end procurement operations process, optimise inventory and supplier performance, and continuously improve the systems and processes that keep our production running smoothly.

Working cross-functionally with Planning, Production, Finance, Culinary, and Operations, you'll play a key role in ensuring the right products are available at the right time, while driving operational excellence and supporting Factor's continued growth.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and develop our Procurement Operations team, responsible for purchasing, supplier coordination, inventory management, and waste reduction.
  • Own the end-to-end procurement operations process, ensuring ingredients and packaging are delivered On Time, In Full, and In Quality (OTIFQ) to support uninterrupted production.
  • Drive inventory governance, ensuing product availability and operational efficiency while minimising waste and stock risk.
  • Champion our zero-waste strategy through continuous optimisation of purchasing parameters, inventory controls, and forecasting inputs.
  • Partner closely with Planning, Finance, Supply Chain, Culinary, and Production to optimize purchasing strategies and ensure smooth day-to-day operations.
  • Monitor procurement KPIs, purchasing data, and system accuracy, using insights to identify trends, resolve discrepancies, and drive operational improvements.
  • Identify opportunities to automate, simplify, and standardise procurement and inventory processes through data, technology, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Develop reporting and dashboards that provide clear visibility of procurement performance, inventory health, supplier performance, and key operational KPIs.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, operational excellence, and data-driven decision making across Procurement Operations.

What you’ll bring

  • At least 5-6 years of relevant work experience in a Supply Chain, Operations, Procurement or Production field
  • Stress resilience and a hands-on approach
  • A proactive, data-driven, and result-oriented mindset
  • Flexibility for occasional weekend work and travel
  • Excellent communication skills, able to work across different teams and cultures
  • Fluency in English (German knowledge is a plus)

What we offer

  • Freedom to initiate, execute and implement your own ideas
  • Lots of learning and development opportunities
  • 24  holidays based on 40 hours per week per year, pro rata
  • A hybrid work setup - with roughly 2 days in our Amsterdam office 
  • Reimbursement of travel expenses to the office
  • Discount on your ClassPass subscription, and a discount for your gym membership via Bedrijfsfitness Nederland 
  • Discount on your additional health insurance through Zilveren Kruis
  • A discount on your weekly, Factor, HelloFresh and/or Green Chef box in the Netherlands
  • Healthy lunches, fruit and snacks in the office 
  • Competitive salary and pension scheme
  • Social activities with our culturally diverse team!

Are you up for the challenge?

After submitting an application our team will review this and get back to you within 5 business days.
